title: Count Subsequences With Non-Decreasing Differences
statement:
You are given an integer array `A` of length `N`.

A **subsequence** is formed by choosing some indices `i1 < i2 < ... < ik` and reading `S = [A[i1], A[i2], ..., A[ik]]`. Two subsequences are different if they use different sets of indices, even when their values are equal.

For a subsequence `S` of length `k ≥ 2`, define its difference array `B` of length `k - 1` by `B[j] = S[j+1] - S[j]`. The subsequence is **good** if `B` is non-decreasing: `B[1] ≤ B[2] ≤ ... ≤ B[k-1]`.

Count the good subsequences of `A`. Only subsequences with length at least `2` are counted (so every pair of indices is good by itself). Since the answer can be very large, print it modulo `10^9 + 7`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `N`.
The second line contains `N` space-separated integers `A[0], ..., A[N-1]` (the line is empty when `N = 0`).
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of good subsequences modulo `10^9 + 7`.

examples.explanation: All 6 pairs are good. Among triples, [1,2,3] has differences 1,1 and [5,2,3] has differences -3,1, so both are good, while [1,5,2] (4,-3) and [1,5,3] (4,-2) are not. The full array has differences 4,-3,1, which is not non-decreasing. Total: 6 + 2 = 8.
Equal values give all differences 0, so every subsequence of length at least 2 is good: 3 pairs plus 1 triple.
No subsequence has length 2 or more.

hints: Define a state by the last two chosen indices (j, i). The difference A[i] - A[j] is the only thing that limits the next choice.

Let cnt[j][i] be the number of good subsequences whose last two elements are at j and i. To extend with index k > i you need A[k] - A[i] ≥ A[i] - A[j], and cnt[i][k] = 1 + the sum of cnt[j][i] over all such j.

Doing this directly is O(N^3). For a fixed middle index i, sort the incoming pairs (j, i) by their difference and take prefix sums; each outgoing pair (i, k) is then answered by a binary search on A[k] - A[i].
